[Aruṇa is represented as the elder brother of Garuḍa, being the son of Vinatā by Kaśyapa. Vinatā prematurely hatched the egg and the child was born without thighs, and hence he is called {%Anūru%} ‘thighless’, or {%Vipāda%} ‘footless’. He cursed his mother that since she had brought him forth before the due season she would be a slave to her rival Kadrū; but at her earnest entreaties, he modified the curse and said that her next son would deliver her from bondage. Aruṇa now holds the office of the charioteer of the Sun. His wife was Śyenī, who bore him two sons Saṃpāti and Jaṭāyu.] .²3 The Sun; रागेण बालारुणकोमलेन <ls>Ku. 3. 30</ls>, <ls n="Ku.">5. 8</ls>; संसृज्यते सरसिजैररुणांशुभिन्नैः; <ls>R. 5. 69</ls>; <ls>Ś. 1. 31</ls> अरुणकररुचायतेऽन्तरीक्षे <ls>Bu. Up. 6. 5. 3</ls>. .{@-णा@} .²1 <ab>N.</ab> of several plants; .³({%a%}) अतिविषा (<lang>Mar.</lang> <ns>अतिविख</ns>); .³({%b%}) Madder (मञ्जिष्ठा); .³({%c%}) त्रिवृत् commonly called Teori; .³({%d%}) a black kind of the same (श्यामाका); .³({%e%}) bitter apple (इन्द्रवारुणी); .³({%f%}) the Gunja plant that yields the red and black berry (गुंज) used as a weight by jewellers <ab>&c.</ab> .³({%g%}) मुण्डतिक्ता <ab>cf.</ab> अरुणः कपिले कुष्ठे सन्ध्यारागेऽर्कसारथौ . अव्यक्तरागे निःशब्दे द्रव्ये त्रिषु निरूपितः . स्त्रियामतिविषाश्यामामञ्जिष्ठात्रिवृतासु च . <ls>Nm.</ls> .²2 <ab>N.</ab> of a river. .{@-णी@} .²1 A red cow (<ls>Nir.</ls>). .²2 The early dawn. .{@-णम्@} .²1 Red colour; दिविस्पृश्यात्यरुणानि कृण्वन् <ls>Rv. 10. 168. 1</ls>. .²2 Gold; अम्भो अरुणं रजतम् <ls>Av. 13. 4. 51</ls>. .²3 Saffron.
